title: Compact Callback Gateway and SDK Ergonomics (Lab)
body:
Purpose:
Quick lab doc proposing a lightweight gateway and SDK ergonomics for handling streamed text + tool callbacks with an emphasis on small frames, observable handshakes, and mobile-friendly fallbacks. This is a working sketch: tradeoffs, telemetry hooks, and rollout suggestions.

Context / problem we're solving:
- Customers building chat and assistant UX want: near-immediate tokens + quick tool results (search, run-code, db-lookup).
- Current SDK patterns either: block until structured tool returns (high latency), or stream raw text then inject tool results as separate messages (brittle reorder + complex client stitching).
- Mobile/embedded clients need tiny payloads, few round trips, and deterministic resume semantics when connectivity drops.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide a compact on-wire protocol (tiny frames) that can carry incremental tokens, tool-call intents, tool-call partial results, and commit markers.
- SDK ergonomics that make client integration trivial: small-memory footprint, explicit resume points, and simple reconcilers for tool outputs.
- Observability: token-level and tool-call-level traces for latency and cost attribution.
- Graceful degradation: if tool call fails or times out, client-visible fallback that avoids janky UX.

Non-goals:
- This is not a full redesign of streaming formats; it's a lab for a small, backwards-compatible gateway / SDK surface we can iterate quickly.

Design overview (high level):
- Compact Callback Gateway (CCG): sits in front of existing streaming runtime. Responsibilities:
  - multiplex stream frames and tool-call frames into compact frames (<= 512B typical).
  - attach stable sequence ids and checkpoint tokens for resume.
  - implement hedged tool-call semantics (fast-path local simulated answer + server resolution).
- SDK adapters (JS, Swift, Kotlin): small runtime that consumes CCG frames, reconciles tool-call placeholders, and exposes a simple event model to apps.

Wire primitives (textual sketch):
- Frame: [seq_id:uint64][checkpoint:string?][kind:byte][payload:bytes] (we'll keep the real wire as newline-delimited JSON for now, but the conceptual fields above make the client logic explicit)
- kind: {0=token, 1=tool-call-start, 2=tool-call-progress, 3=tool-call-complete, 4=commit, 5=error, 6=keepalive} 
- Example JSON frame (human-friendly):
  {"seq":58712, "chk":"c53f", "k":"token", "p":"Hello, th"}
  {"seq":58713, "chk":"c53f", "k":"tool-start", "p":{"tool":"search","call_id":"t-12","meta":"q=..."}}
  {"seq":58714, "chk":"c53f", "k":"tool-progress", "p":{"call_id":"t-12","part":"1/3","payload":"doc id: 42"}}
  {"seq":58715, "chk":"c53f", "k":"tool-complete", "p":{"call_id":"t-12","result":{"title":"...","snippet":"..."}}}
  {"seq":58716, "chk":"d72a", "k":"commit", "p":{"reason":"turn-end"}}

Semantics and client model:
- Sequence monotonicity: seq strictly increases; checkpoint (chk) marks a resume-safe token. Client stores last-seen chk locally for reconnects.
- Tool-call lifecycles: tool-start introduces placeholder in the token stream (e.g., <tool:search:t-12>); token flow can continue while progress frames fill in.
- Tool-progress frames are best-effort partials; clients should render in-place and be prepared to replace partials when complete arrives.
- Commit frames indicate the server considers the turn final; safe to persist analytics / QA sets.

SDK ergonomics (key proposals):
- Event API (minimal): onToken(text, meta), onToolPlaceholder(callId, spec), onToolUpdate(callId, partial), onToolComplete(callId, result), onCommit(checkpoint)
- Integration patterns: app-level component receives tokens and renders incremental transcript; when onToolPlaceholder arrives show a compact spinner/placeholder that reserves a short inline area. Replace with onToolComplete.
- Small-memory client: avoid materializing full transcript; provide cursors for UI to request rehydration from checkpoint boundaries.
- Resume API: connect(chk) to resume from last checkpoint; server will replay from the nearest earlier checkpoint and replay sequence until live. SDK should dedupe frames using seq id to avoid double-applying.

Observability and telemetry hooks (what to capture):
- frame_received(seq, kind, size_bytes, rtt_ms)
- tool_call_started(call_id, tool_name, model_hint, server_region)
- tool_progress(call_id, bytes, elapsed_ms)
- tool_complete(call_id, status, latency_ms, result_size_bytes)
- handshake_resume(chk, reconnected_at)
- client_buffer_underrun(duration_ms) -- for mobile UX debugging

Cost and perf tradeoffs:
- Packing tool partials into streaming increases bandwidth but reduces blocking latency; allow customers to opt-out via policy.
- Gateway needs per-request memory for in-flight tool partials; place a conservative cap (e.g., 64KB) and fall back to non-partial (store-as-artifact) if exceeded.

Fallback / safety behaviors:
- Tool failure policies: on tool timeout -> send tool-complete with status=failed + optional graceful fallback text (model-provided). SDK surfaces a deterministic fallback hook so client can show alternate UI (retry button)
- If checkpoint state mismatches on resume -> gateway emits a short delta-reconciliation frame with explicit replace semantics (seq range to replace).

Compatibility plan (rolling integration):
- Phase 0: lab gateway in sandbox, SDKs in internal feature flag mode. End to end experiments with internal assistant UIs.
- Phase 1: expose pilot for 3 customers (opt-in), metric-driven: latency p50/p95 for turn-to-first-tool-result, error rate for tool reconciliation.
- Phase 2: GA with client libs, enable-by-default for new regions.

Metrics (success criteria):
- primary: median time from user input to first tool-complete visible in client (target: <= 350ms for cached tools, <= 650ms for remote tools in p50)
- reliability: tool-reconciliation error rate < 0.2% for pilot customers
- client CPU/memory: SDK baseline additional memory < 4MB on Android and iOS for typical session
- developer friction: integration time < 2 days for a simple chat widget (measured in pilot onboarding)

Testing plan / QA notes:
- fuzz frames: reorder, duplicate seqs, drop progress frames, simulate partial restarts and check dedupe/replace logic in SDK
- network conditions: 3G/edge, high-loss simulate; ensure resume works and UI doesn't flash jitter
- synthetic load: gateway must enforce per-connection partial caps; smoke test for OOM protection

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODOs):
- wire format: stick with newline JSON vs binary protobuf + compression for mobile. Trade: JSON easier for debugging, binary smaller. We should prototype both but default to JSON for pilot.
- placeholders vs inline structural tokens: do developers prefer opaque call placeholders or inline structured tree nodes? UX research needed.
- hedging semantics: early local simulated answer (cheap heuristic) may confuse deterministic logs. Need to decide visibility in analytics and tests.
- authorization model: tool-call frames can contain sensitive params (db keys). Decide whether gateway should redact payloads in telemetry.

Implementation notes (engineering reminders):
- gateway: language: Rust or Go for small binary, prioritize TLS streaming performance and backpressure handling
- server-side runtime: integrate with existing streaming runtime by adding a thin multiplexer layer; minimal copy semantics preferred
- SDKs: implement common core in TypeScript (for Electron/React Native reuse) and small native wrappers for Swift/Kotlin to minimize platform-specific bugs

Quick UX sketches (words):
- mobile: show incremental tokens; when placeholder arrives show mini-card with dimmed content -> replace when complete; if partial updates arrive, update the card progressively (title then snippet then actions).
- web: allow hover over placeholder to reveal 'waiting for tool' with small progress bar showing number of partials received.

Rollout checklist (short):
- [ ] prototype gateway + js sdk internal demo
- [ ] fuzz tests + resume tests
- [ ] internal perf bench: memory / p99 latency
- [ ] pilot with 3 customers + SDK docs + example app
- [ ] vet telemetry and PII redaction rules with security/compliance

Notes to self / meeting fodder:
- Bring this to streaming sync Wed: focus on resume semantics and telemetry contract
- Ask infra about long-lived streaming connection scaling limits (connection counts)

References and inspiration:
- compact delta frames from prior streaming PRD (see Confluence link above)
- mobile partial rendering patterns (internal design review notes)

If this looks reasonable we'll spin a minimal PoC: gateway that transforms existing streaming outputs into the small frame format, and a JS SDK that renders placeholders and applies dedupe by seq id.
summary: Working draft proposing a compact streaming gateway and SDK event model to support low-latency tool calls and structured incremental updates. Includes wire primitive sketch, SDK API, telemetry hooks, rollout plan, metrics, and open questions.
